I've attached a worksheet with the specific line items (see medivex-rfi-items.xlsx). Can you please provide the items below by end of week?

High-level asks:
- Dataflow diagram showing regional execution and any persistent caches (KV, prefix caching)
- DPA Annex draft or redlines we can circulate internally
- Cross-border transfer controls (EU-US / UK examples): mechanism(s) you rely on and how routing is enforced

- KMS/Key custody approach and HSM usage for customer keys (if supported)

We will share this with legal and security (cc'd). If you can include a short executive summary up front (1–2 pages) calling out residual risks, that helps expedite review. If you need more time, let me know a firm ETA.

Appreciate it —

Elena / team —

Quick technical responses and artifacts attached. I'm answering inline against the items in your workbook where helpful.

1) Dataflow & caching
- Execution: requests are routed by policy at the edge (region tag + customer preference). For Medivex we can pin model execution to EU-only regions or enforce EU-only KV cache residency.
- KV/prefix cache: persistent KV caches live in the same region as the serving cluster by default; we offer an EU-only cache profile that prevents replication to non-EU regions.
- Attachment: dataflow_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram) included in the export-controls-matrix.csv bundle.

2) Cross-border transfer mechanisms
- We support Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and a Data Processing Framework (DPF) offering for enterprise contracts. Routing enforcement is implemented in the request router: policy keys include customer_id, region_preference, and legal_scope. Policy violations are rejected with a 403 and logged.

3) Subprocessors
- Current major subprocessors are listed in our inventory; we can provide an annexed list with scoping by region and function (compute, storage, logging).

4) Audit logs schema & retention
- Logs include request_id, customer_id (hashed), model_version, region_tag, operation, timestamp, latency_ms, token_counts, and event_type.
- Sensitive fields (prompt content) are redacted in logs by default unless customer opts into retention for troubleshooting. Retention default: 90 days; enterprise retention can be configured up to 7 years.

5) KMS/HSM
- Keys: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and a BYOK HSM option for Private deployments. All key operations are audited and accessible in audit logs.

6) Runbook / failover
- We provide a DPF runbook template: primary region routing, healthy-region failover, canary routing for model rollouts, and automatic fallback to language-only model variants under capacity pressure.

Notes / caveats:
- For EU-only legal guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments; hosted multi-region offerings have operational fallbacks that may cross borders in failover scenarios unless pinned.
- Token-level redaction is configurable; we can publish a sample redaction log schema for your security review.

Attachments: export-controls-matrix.csv (matrix + small artefacts bundle).

On Thu I'm available 10:00–12:00 PT if you want the 30-minute walkthrough.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Principal Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: export-controls-matrix.csv (csv)]
